gen-gf-sniglet-gf-monda: Sniglet traces its letters like stitched thread, each terminal stopping short of a curl. Monda keeps every small counter unclogged, which is the clearest thing this pairing has going for it.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-mooli: Distinctive from the first glance, Sniglet looks like a bent paperclip, its line never shifting in weight. Mooli, a sans with open round letters, stays clear at small sizes.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-murecho: Commanding up top, Sniglet is rod stock bent into letters. Murecho, a sans whose s curves open wide at both ends, carries running text along without any snagging or fuss.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-canadian-abo: Sniglet looks like thin steel rod bent into every letter, quiet and level. Noto Sans Canadian Aboriginal, a neutral sans-serif, opens every curve end, and that openness is the pair's best trait.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-cypro-minoan: Commanding and distinctive, Sniglet gives its diagonals the same heft as its verticals. Noto Sans Cypro Minoan cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap, giving the type room to breathe.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-hanifi-rohin: Distinctive, Sniglet makes r, n and m with arches matching their stems. Noto Sans Hanifi Rohingya, a sans-serif with a gaping c, then settles into text with a friendly, modern ease.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-kawi: Flat and distinctive: Sniglet has stroke contrast of exactly none. Noto Sans Kawi is a sans-serif with an open-jawed c like a pair of pliers, and that clarity is the pairing's best quality.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-linear-a: Sniglet has a blunt round-tip marker feel from end to end, terminals stopping short of a curl. And Noto Sans Linear A, a sans-serif with a visibly gaping c at any size, brings clean clarity.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-nko: Noto Sans NKo reads modern and contemporary, its c openings clear enough to see through, a sans with nothing to hide. Sniglet, with strokes like pressed twine, earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoined: Noto Sans NKo Unjoined puts wide openings on small letters, while Sniglet bends cable-like strokes with no swelling or thinning. Over a full page, the text would read approachably and smoothly.
